analysis.title: The 720: 2027 Outlooks: JP Macro & Strategy, KR Strategy, TW Strategy, US Macro, AU Strategy, Global Rates; H-World, China Internet
key_insights: Japan: GS now forecasts three 25 bps BOJ hikes (Dec 2026, Mar 2027, Jun 2027) to a 2.0% terminal rate. The driver is core CPI rapidly exceeding 3.5% through summer 2027 as the government scales back fuel price controls. Real GDP is forecast at +0.9% in CY26 and +1.0% in CY27.

Japan consumption should be supported by solid real wage growth, helped by an April 2027 food consumption tax cut and base pay hikes above 3%. The FY27 primary deficit is forecast to widen to 2.1% of GDP, with limited impact on JGB supply dynamics.

Japan equities: 12-month TOPIX target of 4500, driven by FY27 EPS growth of 9% rather than multiple expansion. GS expects 2027 to be a transitional year with performance broadening beyond AI and banks. Preferred themes are physical AI, energy and resource security, and cybersecurity, plus event-driven restructuring and consolidation.

Japan sector changes: Energy Resources and Commercial & Wholesale Trade raised to Overweight. Banks and IT & Services lowered to Equal Weight on profit-taking risk in financials and AI disruption concerns. Overweights kept on Electrical Appliance & Precision, Machinery, and Steels & Non Ferrous Metals.

Korea: stays Overweight and sees the most upside among regional markets, but cuts the KOSPI target to 7,500 from 9,000 on elevated volatility and slowing earnings momentum. GS forecasts 3.2% GDP growth in 2027, above consensus, on AI-driven memory demand supporting exports and capex.

Korea: GS argues the market prices an excessively bearish view of memory, with the concern spilling into an indiscriminate de-rating of non-memory stocks. Support comes from an estimated US$130bn of corporate buybacks, underinvested positioning and governance reform. Overweight capital goods, tech hardware, health care and internet media. Cautious on financials and domestic consumer names.

Taiwan: downgraded to Marketweight from Overweight and end-2027 TAIEX target cut to 50,000 from 57,500. Reasons are elevated volatility and 85% AI-related market exposure. EPS growth is still forecast at 32% in 2027 and 25% in 2028. GS expects AI growth to peak in 2027, with tighter financing, data-center constraints and elevated margin assumptions raising the risk of later earnings downgrades.

Taiwan valuation and liquidity: the premium to Korea and Tech's record premium to global peers limit re-rating. Rebuilt margin balances and record leveraged ETF exposure make domestic liquidity more procyclical. GS still prefers Tech over non-Tech, with Quality Tech as core holdings and dividend-supported AI Diversifiers as a tactical hedge against Tech-led drawdowns.

US macro: GS forecasts 2027 GDP growth of 2.4% (above consensus) and core PCE inflation falling to 2.4% as the effects of the Iran war, tariffs and AI price pressures fade. Consumption +2.2%, business investment +8% with AI contributing half, wage growth about 3.5%.
US policy path: GS forecasts two more 25 bps Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 to a peak of 4.25-4.5%, then gradual cuts back to 3.25-3.5% starting November 2027.

Australia: GS expects easing financial conditions to improve alpha in 2027 after a record-low-breadth year in which 70% of ASX 200 stocks underperformed. A rate cut is forecast for 4Q27. Banks (premium valuation, fading NIM tailwinds, normalizing credit costs, house price correction) and Mining (near-term earnings downgrades, iron ore downside, positive on copper) face a challenging path. Index-level upside is limited as stock-to-bond valuations have deteriorated.

Global rates: GS expects positive total returns for global bonds in 2027 and fewer central bank hikes than markets price. Year-end 2027 10y targets are UST 4.6%, Gilts 4.8% and Bund 3.1%. 10y JGBs are expected to stay near 2.75% as the BoJ reaches 2% earlier than implied.

Global rates positioning: favor 5y outperformance in the US and Euro area, steepeners in the UK and Germany, and a flatter JGB curve. Prefer owning 10y TIPS on a beta basis versus nominals in the US, and near-dated nominal forwards in Europe and the UK.

Precious metals: GS says 2027 resembles 2022. Rising Fed rates weigh on private investor demand while central bank buying supports gold. Targets are gold $4,650/toz by end-2027 and $5,600/toz by end-2028 once the Fed cuts and Western ETF demand recovers. GS expects near-term downside risk and elevated volatility, and gold to outperform silver in 2027.

Platinum and palladium: persistent US tariff uncertainty keeps supply fragmented and volatility elevated. Rising EV penetration is a structural auto-demand headwind, heavier for platinum as Europe moves away from diesel.

China Internet and AI: evolving US policy to limit Chinese firms' remote access to frontier foreign compute should create a bifurcated AI path. Frontier-model training at maximum scale is constrained while application deployment and inference stay resilient on domestic chips. Vertically integrated giants (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance) are better placed. Independent frontier-model developers face the most uncertainty.

China October activity data weakened broadly and missed expectations. Industrial production slowed to 4.8% YoY (consensus 5.3%), single-month fixed asset investment contracted 16.3% YoY, and retail sales slowed to 0.4% YoY. GS keeps its forecast of 4Q sequential GDP growth slowing to 4.0% QoQ annualized from 4.9%, and expects some 4Q government funds to be deployed in 1Q27.

China e-commerce: GS estimates Double 11 GMV fell about 2% YoY versus about 10% growth last year. October national online retail goods GMV fell 3.6% YoY, the first monthly drop since November 2024. 4Q26E industry online GMV and parcel growth forecasts are cut to 0% and 1%. Temu US GMV growth slowed to 1% YoY in October from 14% in September. Sub-sector preference is Games and Entertainment.

China logistics: tighter social security enforcement is an emerging cost headwind of Rmb4bn to Rmb16bn a year for the industry, with limited ability to raise prices given weak demand and excess capacity. JD Logistics is the only Buy-rated name.

KE Holdings 3Q26: EPS estimates raised 9-13% on gross margin and opex control, revenue estimates cut 1-7%. Existing home transaction volume grew 14% YoY in 3Q and 31% YoY in October across 50 cities. Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 22% YoY. TPs raised to US$25/HK$64.

H World 3Q26: Group EBITDA of Rmb3.1bn beat GS (Rmb2.95bn) and Bloomberg consensus (Rmb2.7-2.8bn), helped by a 13.8% China take rate on supply chain initiatives and SG&A savings. FY26 revenue growth guidance raised to 9-10% YoY. Guides to 700-800 hotel closures over two years. FY26-28E adjusted EBITDA raised 2-5%.

ST Engineering 3Q26: revenue of S$3.4bn rose 9% YoY but missed GS by 3%, which GS attributes to revenue-recognition phasing. Orderbook is a record S$37.7bn, 9M26 OPEX/revenue fell to 9.0% from 10.2% in FY25, and Satcom is on track for positive EBIT in 4Q26.

XPeng 3Q26 first take: operating profit beat GS by 22% on an 8% revenue beat (higher ASPs from exports and carbon credits). GAAP net profit was in line, non-GAAP net profit missed by 18% on a fair value gain reversal. 4Q26 volume guidance of 169k-174k units is 7% above GS and consensus midpoints, and revenue guidance of Rmb30.4bn-31.8bn is 17% above GS and in line with consensus.

Toyo Tire downgraded to Neutral from Buy, TP cut to ¥4,800 from ¥5,500. FY26 operating profit guidance was cut to ¥82bn versus GS ¥90bn and consensus ¥91.3bn, attributed to SAP system disruption and soft tire volumes in Europe and the US. FY26-28 operating profit estimates cut by 7%, 12% and 4%.

KB Financial post-call: 3Q26 earnings restated for regulatory decisions with a net W149bn bottom-line impact, shareholder return unchanged. Bank NIM fell 2bps QoQ to 1.72% on an 8bps rise in funding costs. Management expects BOK hikes to lift loan yields from 4Q26 into 2027. Mid-term ROE target is 13%, and a Value Up plan revisit with minimum dividend guidance is planned next year.

Aspeed management meeting: growth expected from BMC and SMC specification migration, with the 2600 leading 2026 BMC shipments and the 1700 and 2700 lifting 2027 volumes at higher ASPs. The 2800 is targeted to start sampling in 2028, and new SMC products enter mass production in 2H27. Buy, 12m TP NT$22,000.
Korea chart callout: Korea ex-memory stocks trade at a record low 7x NTM P/E.

risk_factors: Japan: higher interest rates and inflation could challenge the economy.
Korea: elevated volatility and slowing earnings momentum.

Taiwan: AI growth rate peaking in 2027, tighter financing, data-center constraints and elevated margin assumptions raise the risk of earnings downgrades. Wide premium to Korea and record Tech premium limit re-rating.
Taiwan domestic liquidity is increasingly procyclical given rebuilt margin balances and record leveraged ETF exposure.
Australia: bank NIM tailwinds fading, credit cost normalization, house price correction and iron ore downside to consensus.
Precious metals: continued Fed hikes weigh on private investor demand. Rising EV penetration weighs on platinum.
China: strong exports versus subdued domestic demand, weak consumer sentiment, and rising social security cost burden for logistics.
China AI: tighter compute-access rules could limit frontier model training and raise regulatory scrutiny of going-global data center operators.
Toyo Tire: SAP system disruption and soft tire volumes in Europe and the US.
